in_text_mentions: In her past history, at the age of 5 months, she began to have papules on the trunk (Figure 2C), and then in one month, papules also developed in the upper and lower extremities on both sides (Figure 2D). panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Clinical photograph of a 3-month-old infant with generalized granulomatous maculopapular rash, a classic early cutaneous manifestation of Blau syndrome. B: Fundus image showing multifocal chorioretinal lesions and pale optic disc consistent with chronic granulomatous panuveitis in Blau syndrome. C: Anterior segment photograph showing subepithelial corneal opacities thought to reflect resorption of prior corneal granulomas in a Blau syndrome patient; no exact vocabulary term for corneal opacity. D: SD-OCT corneal section with asterisks marking subepithelial corneal opacities, corresponding to prior corneal granulomas in Blau syndrome. E: Coronal T2W MRI showing bilateral parotid gland enlargement, attributed to granulomatous inflammation in this Blau syndrome case. F: Coronal post-contrast T1W MRI with fat saturation showing enlarged and infiltrated lacrimal glands in a patient with Blau syndrome.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: H&E section from a Blau syndrome patient shows dermal non-caseating granulomas matching the configured vocabulary. B: LAG immunofluorescence supports macrophage granulomatous infiltrate rather than Langerhans-cell histiocytosis in this Blau syndrome case. C: BerMac-positive macrophage infiltrate demonstrates granulomatous inflammation attributed to Blau syndrome. D: Higher-power H&E of the skin papule from a Blau syndrome patient showing the characteristic non-caseating epithelioid granulomas.

panels.figure_caption: Histological findings. A section of the skin papule was stained with hematoxylin and eosin (A). To characterize the infiltrating epithelioid cells, sequential sections were stained with Langerhans cell-specific LAG antibody (B), macrophage-specific BerMac antibody (C), and hematoxylin and eosin (D). (Original magnification. A, ×200; B–D, ×400).
in_text_mentions: By histological examination of the skin papules, non-caseating epithelioid cell granulomas accompanied with some multinucleated giant cells were observed mainly in the upper dermis around hair follicles (Figure 2A,D). In order to exclude the possibility of Langerhans cell histiocytosis, immunohistochemical studies were performed to reveal that the epithelioid cells were negative for LAG antibody, specific for Langerhans histiocytes (Figure 2B, Langerhans cells in the follicular epidermis were positive), and positive for BerMac antibody, specific for macrophages (Figure 2C).
